newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan gov't to put oil auction revenues aside.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan gov't to put oil auction revenues aside.

text.p: Extraordinary revenues from the auction of 20 marginal oil fields this week will be set aside in a special account and not put towards current government spending, Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
"The revenues will be set aside...until the government decides what to use them for," Petkoff told reporters at the auctions held by state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).
The decision on what to use the funds for would be based on the criteria "that non-recurrent revenues cannot be used to cover ordinary spending," he said.
Venezuela had fallen into the trap of using extraordinary revenues to fund current spending in the past with disastrous consequences, Petkoff said.
Midway through the auction of 20 fields Wednesday, PDVSA had received winning bids totaling over $1.2 billion.
Asked whether some of the money could be used to pay off Venezuela's foreign debt, Petkoff said it was too early to say.
